verses.original: וְ֠נַעֲמָן שַׂר־ צְבָ֨א מֶֽלֶךְ־ אֲרָ֜ם הָיָ֣ה אִישׁ֩ גָּד֨וֹל לִפְנֵ֤י אֲדֹנָיו֙ וּנְשֻׂ֣א פָנִ֔ים כִּֽי־ ב֛וֹ נָֽתַן־ יְהוָ֥ה תְּשׁוּעָ֖ה לַאֲרָ֑ם וְהָאִ֗ישׁ הָיָ֛ה גִּבּ֥וֹר חַ֖יִל מְצֹרָֽע׃
verses.transliteration: wə·na·‘ă·mān śar- ṣə·ḇā me·leḵ- ’ă·rām hā·yāh ’îš gā·ḏō·wl lip̄·nê ’ă·ḏō·nāw ū·nə·śu p̄ā·nîm kî- ḇōw nā·ṯan- Yah·weh tə·šū·‘āh la·’ă·rām wə·hā·’îš hā·yāh gib·bō·wr ḥa·yil mə·ṣō·rā‘
verses.literal: Now Naaman the commander of the army of the king of Aram was a great man in his master’s sight and highly regarded . . . for through him the LORD had given victory to Aram And he was a mighty man of valor but he was a leper
verses.literalPt: Naamã, general do exército do rei da Síria, era um grande homem diante do seu senhor e mui acatado, porque por ele Jeová tinha dado vitória à Síria; era também ilustre em valor, porém leproso.

verses.original: וַאֲרָם֙ יָצְא֣וּ גְדוּדִ֔ים וַיִּשְׁבּ֛וּ מֵאֶ֥רֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל נַעֲרָ֣ה קְטַנָּ֑ה וַתְּהִ֕י לִפְנֵ֖י אֵ֥שֶׁת נַעֲמָֽן׃
verses.transliteration: wa·’ă·rām yā·ṣə·’ū ḡə·ḏū·ḏîm way·yiš·bū mê·’e·reṣ yiś·rā·’êl na·‘ă·rāh qə·ṭan·nāh wat·tə·hî lip̄·nê ’ê·šeṯ na·‘ă·mān
verses.literal: At this time the Arameans had gone out in bands and had taken a young girl from the land of Israel and she was serving . . . Naaman’s wife
verses.literalPt: Os siros tinham feito uma arrancada e da terra de Israel tinham levado cativa uma rapariga pequena, que estava ao serviço da mulher de Naamã.

verses.original: וַתֹּ֙אמֶר֙ אֶל־ גְּבִרְתָּ֔הּ אַחֲלֵ֣י אֲדֹנִ֔י לִפְנֵ֥י הַנָּבִ֖יא אֲשֶׁ֣ר בְּשֹׁמְר֑וֹן אָ֛ז יֶאֱסֹ֥ף אֹת֖וֹ מִצָּרַעְתּֽוֹ׃
verses.transliteration: wat·tō·mer ’el- gə·ḇir·tāh ’a·ḥă·lê ’ă·ḏō·nî lip̄·nê han·nā·ḇî ’ă·šer bə·šō·mə·rō·wn ’āz ye·’ĕ·sōp̄ ’ō·ṯōw miṣ·ṣā·ra‘·tōw
verses.literal: She said to her mistress If only my master would go to the prophet who is in Samaria he would cure him of his leprosy
verses.literalPt: Ela disse à sua senhora: Oxalá que o meu senhor estivesse diante do profeta que está em Samaria! Pois este o curaria da lepra de que padece.

verses.original: וַיָּבֹ֕א וַיַּגֵּ֥ד לַאדֹנָ֖יו לֵאמֹ֑ר כָּזֹ֤את וְכָזֹאת֙ דִּבְּרָ֣ה הַֽנַּעֲרָ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֖ר מֵאֶ֥רֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃
verses.transliteration: way·yā·ḇō way·yag·gêḏ la·ḏō·nāw lê·mōr kā·zōṯ wə·ḵā·zōṯ dib·bə·rāh han·na·‘ă·rāh ’ă·šer mê·’e·reṣ yiś·rā·’êl
verses.literal: And Naaman went and told his master . . . what . . . the girl from the land of Israel had said
verses.literalPt: Então, entrou Naamã e notificou ao seu senhor, dizendo: Assim e assim disse a rapariga que é da terra de Israel.

verses.original: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר מֶֽלֶךְ־ אֲרָם֙ לֶךְ־ בֹּ֔א וְאֶשְׁלְחָ֥ה סֵ֖פֶר אֶל־ מֶ֣לֶךְ יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וַיֵּלֶךְ֩ וַיִּקַּ֨ח בְּיָד֜וֹ עֶ֣שֶׂר כִּכְּרֵי־ כֶ֗סֶף וְשֵׁ֤שֶׁת אֲלָפִים֙ זָהָ֔ב וְעֶ֖שֶׂר חֲלִיפ֥וֹת בְּגָדִֽים׃
verses.transliteration: way·yō·mer me·leḵ- ’ă·rām leḵ- bō wə·’eš·lə·ḥāh sê·p̄er ’el- me·leḵ yiś·rā·’êl way·yê·leḵ way·yiq·qaḥ bə·yā·ḏōw ‘e·śer kik·kə·rê- ḵe·sep̄ wə·šê·šeṯ ’ă·lā·p̄îm zā·hāḇ wə·‘e·śer ḥă·lî·p̄ō·wṯ bə·ḡā·ḏîm
verses.literal: Go now . . . said the king of Aram and I will send you with a letter to the king of Israel So Naaman departed taking with him ten talents of silver six thousand shekels of gold and ten sets of clothing
verses.literalPt: Respondeu o rei da Síria: Vai, anda, e enviarei uma carta ao rei de Israel. Partiu Naamã e levou consigo dez talentos de prata, e seis mil siclos de ouro, e dez mudas de vestidos.

verses.original: וַיָּבֵ֣א הַסֵּ֔פֶר אֶל־ מֶ֥לֶךְ יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל לֵאמֹ֑ר וְעַתָּ֗ה כְּב֨וֹא הַסֵּ֤פֶר הַזֶּה֙ אֵלֶ֔יךָ הִנֵּ֨ה שָׁלַ֤חְתִּי אֵלֶ֙יךָ֙ אֶת־ נַעֲמָ֣ן עַבְדִּ֔י וַאֲסַפְתּ֖וֹ מִצָּרַעְתּֽוֹ׃
verses.transliteration: way·yā·ḇê has·sê·p̄er ’el- me·leḵ yiś·rā·’êl lê·mōr wə·‘at·tāh kə·ḇō·w has·sê·p̄er haz·zeh ’ê·le·ḵā hin·nêh šā·laḥ·tî ’ê·le·ḵā ’eṯ- na·‘ă·mān ‘aḇ·dî wa·’ă·sap̄·tōw miṣ·ṣā·ra‘·tōw
verses.literal: And the letter that he took to the king of Israel stated With this . . . letter I am sending my servant Naaman so that you may cure him of his leprosy
verses.literalPt: Levou a carta ao rei de Israel, a qual dizia: Agora, quando chegar esta carta às tuas mãos, saberás que te enviei o meu servo Naamã, para que o cures da sua lepra.

verses.original: וַיְהִ֡י כִּקְרֹא֩ מֶֽלֶךְ־ יִשְׂרָאֵ֨ל אֶת־ הַסֵּ֜פֶר וַיִּקְרַ֣ע בְּגָדָ֗יו וַיֹּ֙אמֶר֙ הַאֱלֹהִ֥ים אָ֙נִי֙ לְהָמִ֣ית וּֽלְהַחֲי֔וֹת כִּֽי־ זֶה֙ שֹׁלֵ֣חַ אֵלַ֔י לֶאֱסֹ֥ף אִ֖ישׁ מִצָּֽרַעְתּ֑וֹ כִּ֤י אַךְ־ דְּעֽוּ־ נָא֙ וּרְא֔וּ כִּֽי־ מִתְאַנֶּ֥ה ה֖וּא לִֽי׃
verses.transliteration: way·hî kiq·rō me·leḵ- yiś·rā·’êl ’eṯ- has·sê·p̄er way·yiq·ra‘ bə·ḡā·ḏāw way·yō·mer ha·’ĕ·lō·hîm ’ā·nî lə·hā·mîṯ ū·lə·ha·ḥă·yō·wṯ kî- zeh šō·lê·aḥ ’ê·lay le·’ĕ·sōp̄ ’îš miṣ·ṣā·ra‘·tōw kî ’aḵ- də·‘ū- nā ū·rə·’ū kî- miṯ·’an·neh hū lî
verses.literal: When the king of Israel read the letter he tore his clothes and asked Am I God killing and giving life that this man expects me to cure a leper Surely you can . . . see that he is seeking a quarrel with me
verses.literalPt: Tendo o rei de Israel lido a carta, rasgou os seus vestidos e disse: Acaso, sou eu Deus, com poder de tirar e dar vida, para que este me envie um homem, a fim de eu o curar da sua lepra? Mas adverti e vede como anda buscando ocasião para romper comigo.

verses.original: וַיְהִ֞י כִּשְׁמֹ֣עַ׀ אֱלִישָׁ֣ע אִישׁ־ הָאֱלֹהִ֗ים כִּֽי־ קָרַ֤ע מֶֽלֶךְ־ יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ אֶת־ בְּגָדָ֔יו וַיִּשְׁלַח֙ אֶל־ הַמֶּ֣לֶךְ לֵאמֹ֔ר לָ֥מָּה קָרַ֖עְתָּ בְּגָדֶ֑יךָ יָבֹֽא־ נָ֣א אֵלַ֔י וְיֵדַ֕ע כִּ֛י יֵ֥שׁ נָבִ֖יא בְּיִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃
verses.transliteration: way·hî kiš·mō·a‘ ’ĕ·lî·šā‘ ’îš- hā·’ĕ·lō·hîm kî- qā·ra‘ me·leḵ- yiś·rā·’êl ’eṯ- bə·ḡā·ḏāw way·yiš·laḥ ’el- ham·me·leḵ lê·mōr lām·māh qā·ra‘·tā bə·ḡā·ḏe·ḵā yā·ḇō- nā ’ê·lay wə·yê·ḏa‘ kî yêš nā·ḇî bə·yiś·rā·’êl
verses.literal: Now when Elisha the man of God heard that the king of Israel had torn his clothes he sent a message to the king . . . Why have you torn your clothes Please let the man come to me and he will know that there is a prophet in Israel
verses.literalPt: Quando Eliseu, homem de Deus, ouviu que o rei de Israel rasgara os seus vestidos, mandou dizer ao rei: Por que rasgaste os teus vestidos? Que venha ele ter comigo e saberá que há um profeta em Israel.

verses.original: וַיָּבֹ֥א נַעֲמָ֖ן בְּסוּסוֹ וּבְרִכְבּ֑וֹ וַיַּעֲמֹ֥ד פֶּֽתַח־ הַבַּ֖יִת לֶאֱלִישָֽׁע׃
verses.transliteration: way·yā·ḇō na·‘ă·mān bə·sū·sō ū·ḇə·riḵ·bōw way·ya·‘ă·mōḏ pe·ṯaḥ- hab·ba·yiṯ le·’ĕ·lî·šā‘
verses.literal: So Naaman came with his horses and chariots and stood at the door of Elisha’s house
verses.literalPt: Veio Naamã com os seus cavalos e com os seus carros e parou à porta da casa de Eliseu.

verses.original: וַיִּשְׁלַ֥ח אֵלָ֛יו אֱלִישָׁ֖ע מַלְאָ֣ךְ לֵאמֹ֑ר הָל֗וֹךְ וְרָחַצְתָּ֤ שֶֽׁבַע־ פְּעָמִים֙ בַּיַּרְדֵּ֔ן וְיָשֹׁ֧ב בְּשָׂרְךָ֛ לְךָ֖ וּטְהָֽר׃
verses.transliteration: way·yiš·laḥ ’ê·lāw ’ĕ·lî·šā‘ mal·’āḵ lê·mōr hā·lō·wḵ wə·rā·ḥaṣ·tā še·ḇa‘- pə·‘ā·mîm bay·yar·dên wə·yā·šōḇ bə·śā·rə·ḵā lə·ḵā ū·ṭə·hār
verses.literal: Then Elisha sent him a messenger who said Go and wash yourself seven times in the Jordan and your flesh will be restored and you will be clean
verses.literalPt: Eliseu enviou-lhe um mensageiro que lhe dissesse: Vai, e lava-te sete vezes no Jordão, e a tua carne tornará a ti, e ficarás limpo.

verses.original: וַיִּקְצֹ֥ף נַעֲמָ֖ן וַיֵּלַ֑ךְ וַיֹּאמֶר֩ הִנֵּ֨ה אָמַ֜רְתִּי אֵלַ֣י׀ יֵצֵ֣א יָצ֗וֹא וְעָמַד֙ וְקָרָא֙ בְּשֵׁם־ יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהָ֔יו וְהֵנִ֥יף יָד֛וֹ אֶל־ הַמָּק֖וֹם וְאָסַ֥ף הַמְּצֹרָֽע׃
verses.transliteration: way·yiq·ṣōp̄ na·‘ă·mān way·yê·laḵ way·yō·mer hin·nêh ’ā·mar·tî ’ê·lay yê·ṣê yā·ṣō·w wə·‘ā·maḏ wə·qā·rā bə·šêm- Yah·weh ’ĕ·lō·hāw wə·hê·nîp̄ yā·ḏōw ’el- ham·mā·qō·wm wə·’ā·sap̄ ham·mə·ṣō·rā‘
verses.literal: But Naaman went away angry saying . . . I thought that he would surely come out . . . stand and call on the name of the LORD his God and wave his hand over the spot to cure my leprosy
verses.literalPt: Mas Naamã indignou-se e, retirando-se, disse: Eis que pensava eu: ele, com certeza, sairá a ter comigo, pôr-se-á em pé, invocará o nome de Jeová, seu Deus, passará a mão sobre o lugar da lepra e restaurará o leproso.

verses.original: הֲלֹ֡א טוֹב֩ אֲבָנָה וּפַרְפַּ֜ר נַהֲר֣וֹת דַּמֶּ֗שֶׂק מִכֹּל֙ מֵימֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל הֲלֹֽא־ אֶרְחַ֥ץ בָּהֶ֖ם וְטָהָ֑רְתִּי וַיִּ֖פֶן וַיֵּ֥לֶךְ בְּחֵמָֽה׃
verses.transliteration: hă·lō ṭō·wḇ ʾă·ḇå̄·nå̄h ū·p̄ar·par na·hă·rō·wṯ dam·me·śeq mik·kōl mê·mê yiś·rā·’êl hă·lō- ’er·ḥaṣ bā·hem wə·ṭā·hā·rə·tî way·yi·p̄en way·yê·leḵ bə·ḥê·māh
verses.literal: Are not the Abanah and Pharpar the rivers of Damascus better than all the waters of Israel Could I not have washed in them and been cleansed So he turned and went away in a rage
verses.literalPt: Não são, porventura, Abana e Farpar, rios de Damasco, melhores do que todas as águas de Israel? Não me poderia eu lavar neles e ficar limpo? Assim, voltou e se foi enfurecido.

verses.original: וַיִּגְּשׁ֣וּ עֲבָדָיו֮ וַיְדַבְּר֣וּ אֵלָיו֒ וַיֹּאמְר֗וּ אָבִי֙ דָּבָ֣ר גָּד֗וֹל הַנָּבִ֛יא דִּבֶּ֥ר אֵלֶ֖יךָ הֲל֣וֹא תַעֲשֶׂ֑ה וְאַ֛ף כִּֽי־ אָמַ֥ר אֵלֶ֖יךָ רְחַ֥ץ וּטְהָֽר׃
verses.transliteration: way·yig·gə·šū ‘ă·ḇā·ḏāw way·ḏab·bə·rū ’ê·lāw way·yō·mə·rū ’ā·ḇî dā·ḇār gā·ḏō·wl han·nā·ḇî dib·ber ’ê·le·ḵā hă·lō·w ṯa·‘ă·śeh wə·’ap̄ kî- ’ā·mar ’ê·le·ḵā rə·ḥaṣ ū·ṭə·hār
verses.literal: Naaman’s servants, however approached him and said - My father if the prophet had told you to do some great thing would you not have done it How much more, then when he tells you Wash and be cleansed
verses.literalPt: Então, chegaram os seus servos e lhe disseram: Meu pai, se o profeta te houvesse ordenado uma coisa muito difícil, porventura, não haverias feito? Quanto mais, pois, quando ele te diz: Lava-te e fica limpo?

verses.original: וַיֵּ֗רֶד וַיִּטְבֹּ֤ל בַּיַּרְדֵּן֙ שֶׁ֣בַע פְּעָמִ֔ים כִּדְבַ֖ר אִ֣ישׁ הָאֱלֹהִ֑ים וַיָּ֣שָׁב בְּשָׂר֗וֹ כִּבְשַׂ֛ר נַ֥עַר קָטֹ֖ן וַיִּטְהָֽר׃
verses.transliteration: way·yê·reḏ way·yiṭ·bōl bay·yar·dên še·ḇa‘ pə·‘ā·mîm kiḏ·ḇar ’îš hā·’ĕ·lō·hîm way·yā·šāḇ bə·śā·rōw kiḇ·śar na·‘ar qā·ṭōn way·yiṭ·hār
verses.literal: So Naaman went down and dipped himself in the Jordan seven times according to the word of the man of God and his flesh was restored and became like that of a little child and he was clean
verses.literalPt: Desceu ele e mergulhou-se sete vezes no Jordão, conforme a palavra do homem de Deus; a sua carne tornou-se como a carne dum menino pequenino, e ficou limpo.

verses.original: וַיָּשָׁב֩ אֶל־ אִ֨ישׁ הָאֱלֹהִ֜ים ה֣וּא וְכָֽל־ מַחֲנֵ֗הוּ וַיָּבֹא֮ וַיַּעֲמֹ֣ד לְפָנָיו֒ וַיֹּ֗אמֶר הִנֵּה־ נָ֤א יָדַ֙עְתִּי֙ כִּ֣י אֵ֤ין אֱלֹהִים֙ בְּכָל־ הָאָ֔רֶץ כִּ֖י אִם־ בְּיִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וְעַתָּ֛ה קַח־ נָ֥א בְרָכָ֖ה מֵאֵ֥ת עַבְדֶּֽךָ׃
verses.transliteration: way·yā·šāḇ ’el- ’îš hā·’ĕ·lō·hîm hū wə·ḵāl ma·ḥă·nê·hū way·yā·ḇō way·ya·‘ă·mōḏ lə·p̄ā·nāw way·yō·mer hin·nêh- nā yā·ḏa‘·tî kî ’ên ’ĕ·lō·hîm bə·ḵāl hā·’ā·reṣ kî ’im- bə·yiś·rā·’êl wə·‘at·tāh qaḥ- nā ḇə·rā·ḵāh mê·’êṯ ‘aḇ·de·ḵā
verses.literal: Then Naaman and all his attendants . . . went back to the man of God stood before him and declared Now I know for sure that there is no God in all the earth except . . . in Israel So please accept a gift from your servant
verses.literalPt: Voltou ao homem de Deus, ele e toda a sua comitiva, e veio, e se apresentou diante de Eliseu, e disse: Eis, agora, sei que em toda a terra não há Deus senão em Israel; agora, recebe do teu servo um presente.

verses.original: וַיֹּ֕אמֶר חַי־ יְהוָ֛ה אֲשֶׁר־ עָמַ֥דְתִּי לְפָנָ֖יו אִם־ אֶקָּ֑ח וַיִּפְצַר־ בּ֥וֹ לָקַ֖חַת וַיְמָאֵֽן׃
verses.transliteration: way·yō·mer ḥay- Yah·weh ’ă·šer- ‘ā·maḏ·tî lə·p̄ā·nāw ’im- ’eq·qāḥ way·yip̄·ṣar- bōw lā·qa·ḥaṯ way·mā·’ên
verses.literal: But Elisha replied As surely as the LORD lives before whom I stand I will not accept it And although Naaman urged him to accept it he refused
verses.literalPt: Mas ele respondeu: Pela vida de Jeová, em cuja presença estou, não o receberei. Instou com ele para que o tomasse, mas ele recusou.

verses.original: וַיֹּאמֶר֮ נַעֲמָן֒ וָלֹ֕א יֻתַּן־ נָ֣א לְעַבְדְּךָ֔ מַשָּׂ֥א צֶֽמֶד־ פְּרָדִ֖ים אֲדָמָ֑ה כִּ֡י לֽוֹא־ יַעֲשֶׂה֩ ע֨וֹד עַבְדְּךָ֜ עֹלָ֤ה וָזֶ֙בַח֙ לֵאלֹהִ֣ים אֲחֵרִ֔ים כִּ֖י אִם־ לַיהוָֽה׃
verses.transliteration: way·yō·mer na·‘ă·mān wā·lō yut·tan- nā lə·‘aḇ·də·ḵā maś·śā ṣe·meḏ- pə·rā·ḏîm ’ă·ḏā·māh kî lō·w- ya·‘ă·śeh ‘ō·wḏ ‘aḇ·də·ḵā ‘ō·lāh wā·ze·ḇaḥ lê·lō·hîm ’ă·ḥê·rîm kî ’im- Yah·weh
verses.literal: If you will not said Naaman please let me, your servant, be given as much soil as a pair of mules can carry For your servant will never again make a burnt offering or a sacrifice to any other god but the LORD
verses.literalPt: Disse Naamã: Se não, rogo-te que se me dê da terra do país quanta baste para carregar duas mulas; pois daqui avante o teu servo não oferecerá holocausto nem sacrifício a outros deuses, senão a Jeová.

verses.original: לַדָּבָ֣ר הַזֶּ֔ה יִסְלַ֥ח יְהוָ֖ה לְעַבְדֶּ֑ךָ בְּב֣וֹא אֲדֹנִ֣י בֵית־ רִמּוֹן֩ לְהִשְׁתַּחֲוֺ֨ת שָׁ֜מָּה וְה֣וּא׀ נִשְׁעָ֣ן עַל־ יָדִ֗י וְהִֽשְׁתַּחֲוֵ֙יתִי֙ בֵּ֣ית רִמֹּ֔ן בְּהִשְׁתַּחֲוָיָ֙תִי֙ בֵּ֣ית רִמֹּ֔ן יִסְלַח־ נא יְהוָ֥ה לְעַבְדְּךָ֖ בַּדָּבָ֥ר הַזֶּֽה׃
verses.transliteration: lad·dā·ḇār haz·zeh yis·laḥ Yah·weh lə·‘aḇ·de·ḵā bə·ḇō·w ’ă·ḏō·nî ḇêṯ- rim·mō·wn lə·hiš·ta·ḥă·wōṯ šām·māh wə·hū niš·‘ān ‘al- yā·ḏî wə·hiš·ta·ḥă·wê·ṯî bêṯ rim·mōn bə·hiš·ta·ḥă·wā·yā·ṯî bêṯ rim·mōn yis·laḥ- n Yah·weh lə·‘aḇ·də·ḵā bad·dā·ḇār haz·zeh
verses.literal: Yet may the LORD forgive your servant this one thing When my master goes into the temple of Rimmon to worship there and he leans on my arm and I bow down in the temple of Rimmon - may the LORD forgive your servant in this matter
verses.literalPt: Nisto perdoe Jeová ao teu servo: quando meu amo entrar na casa de Rimom para ali adorar e se encostar na minha mão, e eu me prostrar na casa de Rimom, perdoe Jeová ao teu servo, quando ali me prostrar.

verses.original: וַיֹּ֥אמֶר ל֖וֹ לֵ֣ךְ לְשָׁל֑וֹם וַיֵּ֥לֶךְ מֵאִתּ֖וֹ כִּבְרַת־ אָֽרֶץ׃ס
verses.transliteration: way·yō·mer lōw lêḵ lə·šā·lō·wm way·yê·leḵ mê·’it·tōw kiḇ·raṯ- ’ā·reṣ
verses.literal: Go in peace said Elisha But after Naaman had traveled . . . a short distance
verses.literalPt: Eliseu disse-lhe: Vai-te em paz. Retirou-se dele uma pequena distância.

verses.original: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר גֵּיחֲזִ֗י נַעַר֮ אֱלִישָׁ֣ע אִישׁ־ הָאֱלֹהִים֒ הִנֵּ֣ה׀ חָשַׂ֣ךְ אֲדֹנִ֗י אֶֽת־ נַעֲמָ֤ן הָֽאֲרַמִּי֙ הַזֶּ֔ה מִקַּ֥חַת מִיָּד֖וֹ אֵ֣ת אֲשֶׁר־ הֵבִ֑יא חַי־ יְהוָה֙ כִּֽי־ אִם־ רַ֣צְתִּי אַחֲרָ֔יו וְלָקַחְתִּ֥י מֵאִתּ֖וֹ מְאֽוּמָה׃
verses.transliteration: way·yō·mer gê·ḥă·zî na·‘ar ’ĕ·lî·šā‘ ’îš- hā·’ĕ·lō·hîm hin·nêh ḥā·śaḵ ’ă·ḏō·nî ’eṯ- na·‘ă·mān hā·’ă·ram·mî haz·zeh miq·qa·ḥaṯ mî·yā·ḏōw ’êṯ ’ă·šer- hê·ḇî ḥay- Yah·weh kî- ’im- raṣ·tî ’a·ḥă·rāw wə·lā·qaḥ·tî mê·’it·tōw mə·’ū·māh
verses.literal: Gehazi the servant of Elisha the man of God said Look my master has spared this Aramean Naaman by not accepting . . . what he brought As surely as the LORD . . . . . . lives I will run after him and get something from him
verses.literalPt: Mas Geazi, criado do homem de Deus, disse: Eis que o meu amo poupou a este Naamã, siro, não recebendo das mãos dele o que trouxe; pela vida de Jeová, correrei atrás dele e receberei dele alguma coisa.

verses.original: וַיִּרְדֹּ֥ף גֵּיחֲזִ֖י אַחֲרֵ֣י נַֽעֲמָ֑ן וַיִּרְאֶ֤ה נַֽעֲמָן֙ רָ֣ץ אַחֲרָ֔יו וַיִּפֹּ֞ל מֵעַ֧ל הַמֶּרְכָּבָ֛ה לִקְרָאת֖וֹ וַיֹּ֥אמֶר הֲשָׁלֽוֹם׃
verses.transliteration: way·yir·dōp̄ gê·ḥă·zî ’a·ḥă·rê na·‘ă·mān way·yir·’eh na·‘ă·mān rāṣ ’a·ḥă·rāw way·yip·pōl mê·‘al ham·mer·kā·ḇāh liq·rā·ṯōw way·yō·mer hă·šā·lō·wm
verses.literal: So Gehazi pursued Naaman And when Naaman saw him running toward him he got down from the chariot to meet him and asked Is everything all right
verses.literalPt: Então, foi Geazi em alcance de Naamã. Quando Naamã viu alguém correndo atrás dele, saltou do carro a recebê-lo e perguntou: Vai tudo bem?

verses.original: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר׀ שָׁל֗וֹם אֲדֹנִי֮ שְׁלָחַ֣נִי לֵאמֹר֒ הִנֵּ֣ה עַתָּ֡ה זֶ֠ה בָּ֣אוּ אֵלַ֧י שְׁנֵֽי־ נְעָרִ֛ים מֵהַ֥ר אֶפְרַ֖יִם מִבְּנֵ֣י הַנְּבִיאִ֑ים תְּנָה־ נָּ֤א לָהֶם֙ כִּכַּר־ כֶּ֔סֶף וּשְׁתֵּ֖י חֲלִפ֥וֹת בְּגָדִֽים׃
verses.transliteration: way·yō·mer šā·lō·wm ’ă·ḏō·nî šə·lā·ḥa·nî lê·mōr hin·nêh ‘at·tāh zeh bā·’ū ’ê·lay šə·nê- nə·‘ā·rîm mê·har ’ep̄·ra·yim mib·bə·nê han·nə·ḇî·’îm tə·nāh- nā lā·hem kik·kar- ke·sep̄ ū·šə·tê ḥă·li·p̄ō·wṯ bə·ḡā·ḏîm
verses.literal: Everything is all right Gehazi replied My master has sent me to say Look two young men from the sons of the prophets have just now . . . come to me from the hill country of Ephraim Please give them a talent of silver and two sets of clothing
verses.literalPt: Respondeu ele: Tudo vai bem. Meu amo enviou-me a dizer: Eis que agora mesmo são chegados a mim da região montanhosa de Efraim dois moços dos filhos dos profetas; dá-lhes um talento de prata e duas mudas de vestidos.

verses.original: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר נַעֲמָ֔ן הוֹאֵ֖ל קַ֣ח כִּכָּרָ֑יִם וַיִּפְרָץ־ בּ֗וֹ וַיָּצַר֩ כִּכְּרַ֨יִם כֶּ֜סֶף בִּשְׁנֵ֣י חֲרִטִ֗ים וּשְׁתֵּי֙ חֲלִפ֣וֹת בְּגָדִ֔ים וַיִּתֵּן֙ אֶל־ שְׁנֵ֣י נְעָרָ֔יו וַיִּשְׂא֖וּ לְפָנָֽיו׃
verses.transliteration: way·yō·mer na·‘ă·mān hō·w·’êl qaḥ kik·kā·rā·yim way·yip̄·rāṣ- bōw way·yā·ṣar kik·kə·ra·yim ke·sep̄ biš·nê ḥă·ri·ṭîm ū·šə·tê ḥă·li·p̄ō·wṯ bə·ḡā·ḏîm way·yit·tên ’el- šə·nê nə·‘ā·rāw way·yiś·’ū lə·p̄ā·nāw
verses.literal: But Naaman insisted Please take two talents And he urged Gehazi to accept them Then he tied up two talents of silver in two bags along with two sets of clothing and gave them to two of his servants who carried them ahead of Gehazi
verses.literalPt: Disse Naamã: Sê servido de tomar dois talentos. Instou com ele, e atou dois talentos de prata juntamente com duas mudas de vestidos em dois sacos, e pô-los sobre dois dos seus servos, que os levaram diante de Geazi.

verses.original: וַיָּבֹא֙ אֶל־ הָעֹ֔פֶל וַיִּקַּ֥ח מִיָּדָ֖ם וַיִּפְקֹ֣ד בַּבָּ֑יִת וַיְשַׁלַּ֥ח אֶת־ הָאֲנָשִׁ֖ים וַיֵּלֵֽכוּ׃
verses.transliteration: way·yā·ḇō ’el- hā·‘ō·p̄el way·yiq·qaḥ mî·yā·ḏām way·yip̄·qōḏ bab·bā·yiṯ way·šal·laḥ ’eṯ- hā·’ă·nā·šîm way·yê·lê·ḵū
verses.literal: When Gehazi came to the hill he took the gifts from the servants and stored them in the house Then he dismissed the men and they departed
verses.literalPt: Tendo ele chegado ao outeiro, tomou-os das mãos deles e depositou-os na casa; e despediu os homens, que se foram.

verses.original: וְהוּא־ בָא֙ וַיַּעֲמֹ֣ד אֶל־ אֲדֹנָ֔יו וַיֹּ֤אמֶר אֵלָיו֙ אֱלִישָׁ֔ע מֵאָן גֵּחֲזִ֑י וַיֹּ֕אמֶר לֹֽא־ הָלַ֥ךְ עַבְדְּךָ֖ אָ֥נֶה וָאָֽנָה׃
verses.transliteration: wə·hū- ḇā way·ya·‘ă·mōḏ ’el- ’ă·ḏō·nāw way·yō·mer ’ê·lāw ’ĕ·lî·šā‘ mē·ʾå̄n gê·ḥă·zî way·yō·mer lō- hā·laḵ ‘aḇ·də·ḵā ’ā·neh wā·’ā·nāh
verses.literal: When Gehazi went in and stood before his master Elisha asked him Gehazi where have you been Your servant did not go anywhere . . . he replied
verses.literalPt: Ele, porém, entrou e pôs-se diante do seu amo. Perguntou-lhe Eliseu: Donde vens, Geazi? Respondeu ele: Teu servo não foi a parte alguma.

verses.original: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר אֵלָיו֙ לֹא־ לִבִּ֣י הָלַ֔ךְ כַּאֲשֶׁ֧ר הָֽפַךְ־ אִ֛ישׁ מֵעַ֥ל מֶרְכַּבְתּ֖וֹ לִקְרָאתֶ֑ךָ הַעֵ֞ת לָקַ֤חַת אֶת־ הַכֶּ֙סֶף֙ וְלָקַ֣חַת בְּגָדִ֔ים וְזֵיתִ֤ים וּכְרָמִים֙ וְצֹ֣אן וּבָקָ֔ר וַעֲבָדִ֖ים וּשְׁפָחֽוֹת׃
verses.transliteration: way·yō·mer ’ê·lāw lō- lib·bî hā·laḵ ka·’ă·šer hā·p̄aḵ- ’îš mê·‘al mer·kaḇ·tōw liq·rā·ṯe·ḵā ha·‘êṯ lā·qa·ḥaṯ ’eṯ- hak·ke·sep̄ wə·lā·qa·ḥaṯ bə·ḡā·ḏîm wə·zê·ṯîm ū·ḵə·rā·mîm wə·ṣōn ū·ḇā·qār wa·‘ă·ḇā·ḏîm ū·šə·p̄ā·ḥō·wṯ
verses.literal: But Elisha questioned him . . . Did not my spirit go with you when the man got down from his chariot to meet you Is this the time to accept money . . . and clothing olive groves and vineyards sheep and oxen menservants and maidservants
verses.literalPt: Replicou-lhe Eliseu: Porventura, não foi contigo o meu coração, quando o homem voltou do seu carro ao teu encontro? Era a ocasião para receberes dinheiro e para receberes vestidos, e olivais, e vinhas, e ovelhas, e bois, e servos, e servas?

verses.original: וְצָרַ֤עַת נַֽעֲמָן֙ תִּֽדְבַּק־ בְּךָ֔ וּֽבְזַרְעֲךָ לְעוֹלָ֑ם וַיֵּצֵ֥א מִלְּפָנָ֖יו מְצֹרָ֥ע כַּשָּֽׁלֶג׃ס
verses.transliteration: wə·ṣā·ra·‘aṯ na·‘ă·mān tiḏ·baq- bə·ḵā ū·ḇə·zar·‘ă·ḵā lə·‘ō·w·lām way·yê·ṣê mil·lə·p̄ā·nāw mə·ṣō·rā‘ kaš·šā·leḡ
verses.literal: Therefore, the leprosy of Naaman will cling to you and your descendants forever And as Gehazi left his presence he was leprous as white as snow
verses.literalPt: Portanto, a lepra de Naamã se pegará a ti e à tua semente para sempre. Geazi saiu da presença de Eliseu branco de lepra como a neve.
